likely_cause.reasoning: The domain is not lapsed: RDAP shows it registered in 1997, paid to 2028-02-16, registrar Network Solutions, status clientTransferProhibited, nameservers at HostGator (so it is hosted, not parked). The Wayback Machine has a normal business homepage ('Home - Falco Design', canonical https://falcodesign.com/) captured on 2025-09-26, with no casino or redirect strings in the archived HTML. Today the same domain serves a WordPress 'critical error' page (HTTP 500) to direct requests and sends Chrome visitors to tr.l-bahiscasino-l.cam, a gambling domain. A live WordPress site that suddenly redirects browsers to gambling spam while returning errors to direct requests is the usual pattern of an injected redirect on a compromised install (inference - no source states the business was hacked). The HTTP 500 also points to a WordPress or hosting fault, which may be part of the same incident or separate.

fix_steps.step: Log in to the Network Solutions registrar account and the HostGator hosting account, confirm both are still under the studio's control, enable two-factor authentication and confirm the 2028 renewal and current nameservers.

Take the broken WordPress install offline (or restore from a backup made before October 2025), then change every hosting, WordPress admin, FTP/SFTP, database and mailbox password and reinstall core, theme and plugins from clean copies.

After cleanup, re-test the homepage in a browser and by direct request to confirm no redirect remains, ask the host to run a malware scan, and request a review in Google Search Console if the domain is verified there.
While the site is down, change or remove the website link on the Google Business Profile (and the Instagram bio and about.me profile) so customers are not sent to the gambling domain.
Rebuild or restore a short, clean site - services, a few portfolio pieces, contact details, a tap-to-call button and a quote form - before re-linking it from Google, Instagram and about.me.
Add basic monitoring: uptime checks, weekly backups, automatic WordPress updates and an SSL/malware alert so a repeat failure is noticed quickly.

audit_md:
# Website Health Check: Falco Design

## What we saw on 13 November 2026
- The Google Business Profile lists falcodesign.com as the website, phone (732) 390-0099, category "Website designer", rating 3.7.
- In Chrome, falcodesign.com left the studio's site and landed on tr.l-bahiscasino-l.cam, an unrelated gambling domain that itself shows a Cloudflare 522 timeout (screenshots at desktop and 390 px).
- A direct request to the same domain returned HTTP 500 with a WordPress "critical error" page, so the redirect is added for browser visits rather than every request (inference).
- The domain is paid up (registered 1997, expires 16 Feb 2028, Network Solutions, HostGator nameservers); the last archived copy of the real homepage is 26 Sep 2025.

## What it means for customers
Anyone clicking the website link on Google, Instagram or about.me gets an error page for a gambling site instead of examples of the studio's work. Until it is fixed, the phone number on the Google profile is the dependable way to reach Falco Design.

## How to fix it
1. Check the Network Solutions registrar and HostGator hosting accounts, enable two-factor authentication and confirm renewals. Owner, 1-2 hours.
2. Take the WordPress install offline or restore a backup from before October 2025, then change all hosting, WordPress, database and mailbox passwords. Developer or host, 3-8 hours.
3. Re-test for redirects in a browser and by direct request, ask the host for a malware scan and request a Search Console review. Developer, 1-2 hours.
4. Meanwhile, remove or repoint the website link on Google, Instagram and about.me. Owner, 0.5-1 hour.
5. Rebuild a short clean site with services, portfolio, tap-to-call and a quote form, then re-link it. Designer or developer, 8-20 hours.

## After the fix
Maps still offers "Add missing information" and "Add a photo", shows no street address, and the rating is 3.7. Completing the profile and asking recent clients for reviews is a small follow-up that helps in local search.

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.

Best regards,
[Name], [Consultancy]

## Open questions
- Who holds the Network Solutions registrar login, and who holds the HostGator hosting or cPanel login?

caveats: Effort hours are our rough estimates, not quotes or commitments; no prices are stated because no source gave any.
The cause is an inference from public records (RDAP, Wayback, live test). No source states that the site was hacked, and we did not inspect server logs or files.
The redirect appears in a real Chrome browser but not in plain HTTP requests, which suggests a conditional server-side rule; the mechanism could not be confirmed without access to the site.
Google Maps showed 'You're seeing a limited view of Google Maps' without sign-in, so review text and dates were not readable.
